parts.text:
Job: plan. Seat: drafter.

Paths you give a tool:
- a path such as closure/memo.md or evidence/ is in the finding folder you are given;
- kit/ and a page's path in the kit, such as kit/assistant/README.md, is one of the kit's Markdown pages, read only;

This job may write plan.md: the rows of its table below the header row, and the lines below the table. The lines above the table and its header row stay as they are.
Any other write, and any read outside these paths, is refused and recorded.
When the job is done, reply with a short summary and call no tool.

system_instruction:
You sit in the drafter seat. You draft, and a person in the owner seat corrects, rules and signs.

Your job is to draft the plan for the finding folder you are given. Follow assistant/draft-plan.md in the kit, and the rules for every job in assistant/README.md.

You may write the rows of the table in plan.md below its header row, and the lines below that table. You may write nothing else, inside the finding folder or outside it. You may read the finding folder and the kit's pages.

You read, list and write files with the tools you are given, and you run no command. When you say you are done, the loop runs finding check and may hand its page back to you once. Put anything the procedure leaves to a person in your final message, as a question for the owner.

functionDeclarations.name: list_files
functionDeclarations.description: List files, with each file's size in bytes. Give no path for the whole finding folder, a folder inside it such as evidence, kit for the kit's Markdown pages, run for the run pages this seat may read, or out for this job's output folder.

path.description: The folder to list. Leave it out for the finding folder.

functionDeclarations.name: read_file
functionDeclarations.description: Read one file. A Markdown or text file comes back as its text. A PDF, Word, Excel, CSV or email file in the finding folder comes back page by page as the check reads it, under headings such as ## Page 2, and names any page the reader found no text on.

path.description: The file, such as evidence/EV-07 report.pdf or kit/assistant/README.md.

page.description: Return only this page of a PDF, Word, Excel, CSV or email file.

functionDeclarations.name: write_file
functionDeclarations.description: Write a whole file, replacing what was there. Only the paths this job may write are accepted. Any other write is refused, changes nothing and is recorded.

content.description: The whole new text of the file.

# Drafting procedures for an AI assistant

RegRem Engine checks the proof and an AI assistant the financial institution allows drafts it. These pages are the written procedure for each drafting job, one page a job, written for any assistant and naming none. Give the assistant the page and the finding folder, then run the check on what it wrote. Commands run from the kit root, and `finding` stands for `finding/finding`, or `py -I finding\finding.py` on Windows.

| Job | Page | What it writes | What it has to pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Turn the letter into a plan | [draft-plan.md](draft-plan.md) | plan.md | `finding check` prints no "Not ready" line |
| Describe each evidence file | [draft-covers.md](draft-covers.md) | the What and For lines of each cover | `finding check` counts every file |
| Draft the closure memo | [draft-memo.md](draft-memo.md) | closure/memo.md | every row on the list gets a person's ruling or a fix |
| Propose a ruling for each row | [propose-rulings.md](propose-rulings.md) | closure/proposed-rulings.md | a person copies the ones they accept |
| Answer internal audit's questions | [answer-audit.md](answer-audit.md) | a draft answer outside the record | each answer cites the folder |

## The rules for every job

1. The assistant drafts, and a person decides. It never types a Signed by, Produced by, Approved by, Never signed or Status line, never writes closure/rulings.md or closure/record.md, and never runs `finding sign`.
2. It works only inside the finding folder, on a machine and a service the institution has approved for that information. If the institution allows no assistant for a supervisory finding, a person does these jobs by hand, and the check works the same.
3. It copies nothing from the finding folder to anywhere outside it.
4. Every figure, date and quotation it writes carries a cite to the page it came from, in digits and full dates so the check can read it. A claim it cannot cite goes in as a question for a person.
5. The check reads what it wrote and gives the same answer every run. Run `finding check` after every job. Until a person signs the covers, each draft cover is one row saying how many claims match its pages, so read the other rows as the test of the draft: a claim that does not match keeps its own row, and the assistant fixes it or asks. Once the covers are signed, the whole list is the test. Run `finding eval` when the memo is ready, because it plants errors in the claims that match a draft's pages too. A wrong figure that sits on the cited page still ties, so a person reads each sentence against its page.

## How these pages improve

A miss a reviewer catches can become two things. One is a change to the procedure page, written in general terms. The other is an invented case in [library/cases](../library/README.md), which every later release has to pass. Neither carries anything from an institution's folder, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) says how to propose one.

# Draft the plan

Goal: turn the Supervisor's letter into plan.md, one row per milestone, for the finding owner to correct.

Reads: finding.md, the letter as pasted, with its five parts: Concern, Cause, Consequence, Corrective action, Commitment. Also the board minutes E-PLAN-1 or the financial institution's written answer if the folder holds them, read to the last page, because a later page may amend an owner or a date.

Writes: rows in the table in plan.md, under its header row. Leave the header row as it is. Each row has six cells:

```text
| M1 Short name of the milestone | Owner role | 2026-02-28 | What is true when done | EV-03, EV-04 (done) | What internal audit will test |
```

## Rules

- Start each milestone with its id, M1, M2 and so on. Keep each to one thing a person can show evidence for.
- Use a date from the letter or the institution's written answer. If the letter gives no date for a step, write the date as a question below the table for the finding owner, and leave the row out until there is one.
- The check does not compare plan.md with the minutes or the institution's answer, so a wrong owner or date passes it. Take each owner and date from the latest page that sets it, and name that page in a line under the table.
- Use a role in the owner cell. A person's name in a cell can trip the deny list and must never leave the institution.
- Number the evidence ids and keep them stable. Later covers and memo cites use the same ids.
- List every file that shows the milestone done in its Evidence cell, the file that completes it included, such as a lookback's final report. A file that does not exist yet gets an evidence id now, kept for it, such as EV-61. The check keeps the milestone unsigned while that file is missing. A row that lists only the methodology and its approval reads as signed once those two are, however much of the work is left.
- Mark the file that completes the milestone with `(done)` after its id, as in `EV-60, EV-61 (done)`, and reserve that id with its mark before the file exists. Mark one file a row. The milestone's date and its lateness then come from that file, such as a training roster's last completion date. Every other file the row lists still has to be signed. Without the mark, a report signed three days after the work ended makes the milestone read three days later than all the institution's papers say. Keep every file that shows the milestone done in its Evidence cell, and let the mark set the date.
- Answer every sentence of the Cause and Corrective action. Under the table, write one line per sentence naming its milestone or the reason it needs none, so the owner can see nothing was dropped.
- Write what internal audit will test as something a person can test: a sample, a recomputation, a comparison.
- Never say the finding is closed. Until the record holds the issuer's entry, such a line is a row on the list that stops the signature, and no ruling clears it, so it has to be reworded. Any other use of the word closed goes on the list for the owner to rule on.

## Passing

`finding check` prints no "Not ready" line. The screen shows the plan's dates marked proposed until the board's minutes, E-PLAN-1, are signed. The finding owner corrects the rows, and the board approves.

# Finding MRA-PAM-05
Identifier: MRA-PAM-05
Institution: Tallowmere Bank
Issuer: the Supervisor
Letter date: 2026-01-20
Kind of matter: supervisory finding
Owner role: Chief Information Security Officer

## Concern

The bank does not control privileged access to its systems. In the second half of 2025 the Supervisor found leavers, employees and contractors alike, whose privileged accounts stayed active for weeks after they left, privileged accounts with no named owner, and no regular review of who holds privileged access.

## Cause

The access management standard set no deadline for removing a leaver's access. The HR system did not tell the identity team when an employee left, and contractor leavers were reported by email when someone remembered. No one reviewed privileged access on a schedule, and the people who would review it were never trained.

## Consequence

Former staff and contractors could have used privileged access after they left, and accounts that no one owned could have been used without anyone noticing. The board could not be told how many people held privileged access or whether they still needed it.

## Corrective action

The bank must revise its access management standard to set a deadline for removing a leaver's access and to require a quarterly review of privileged access; automate leaver notices from the HR system and remove the access of every leaver, employee or contractor, within one business day; remove, or assign a named owner to, every privileged account that has none; train every reviewer before they review and complete a first quarterly review of privileged access; and extend the quarterly review to the cloud hosting platform.

## Commitment

The bank must send the Supervisor a written remediation plan approved by its board within 30 days of this letter, with an owner role and a committed date for each action. The Supervisor will consider the matter for closure only after internal audit has tested the remediation.

result:
# finding: one folder per finding

When your financial institution tells the board and the Supervisor that a finding is fixed, code has checked every figure and date written in digits, every quotation and every document in the closure package against its evidence. Whatever did not check sits on a one-page list with a role against it. The finding owner signs, internal audit tests the fix, the issuer closes, internal audit for its own findings and the Supervisor for its own, and nothing about the finding leaves the institution.

Everything in `cases/` is invented.

## The folder

```
MRA-CMP-07/
  finding.md           the Supervisor's letter
  plan.md              one row per milestone
  evidence/            one file per piece
  closure/memo.md      the closure memo
  closure/rulings.md   rulings on the list
  closure/record.md    board approval, signature, closers
  closure/measures.md  hours booked, and what internal audit sent back
  closure/finding-log.jsonl   one line for each corrected paste or restarted record
  .finding-state.json  hashes, deny list, signature
```

Copy a folder with `cp -R folder copy`. `cp -R folder/* copy` drops the dot file, and with it the record of signed files.

`new` takes a path whose last part is the finding's id, makes the folder there and writes the templates, with no SYNTHETIC line to delete. It refuses a path inside the kit's own folders, so an institution's finding never lands in the kit. An evidence file opens with four lines:

```
What: EV-07 Complaint intake procedure
For: M2 EV-07
Signed by: Head of Complaints, 2026-03-14
Status: FINAL
```

The lines may sit in any order, together at the top of the file, and a blank line ends them. `Revised: YYYY-MM-DD` records a later change, `Source:` says where the text came from, and `Checked by:` names a second person who compared a typed page. `finding covers` also writes a Source line and a comment.

Signed by is one of four signature lines, and a person types the one that fits the file:

- `Signed by: Head of Complaints, 2026-03-14` for a document a person signs, such as a procedure, minutes, an attestation or a report a person issues.
- `Produced by: case manager aging report, 2026-04-30` for system output, such as an MI workbook or a data extract, on the as-at date a person confirmed.
- `Approved by: EV-29` for a document the institution approved by a separate record, such as a method approved by email, naming that record's evidence id.
- `Never signed: training deck` for material an institution never signs, such as a quick reference card. Its ties count, and it never counts toward a milestone.

System output, such as a monthly MI workbook, a system aging report or a data extract, comes from a system as at a date. Its cover gives that system or report and the as-at date a person confirmed, in place of the Signed by line:

```
Produced by: case manager aging report, 2026-04-30
```

An institution often approves a document by a separate record, such as a QA method approved by email, a lookback method approved on a signed sheet or an MI pack accepted in a resolved minute. The document's cover then names that record's evidence id in place of the Signed by line, and the record gets its own cover, signed by the role that approved:

```
Approved by: EV-29
```

The document counts as signed on the record's date once the record is present and signed by a person. A record that is missing, unsigned or changed leaves the document unsigned with that reason, as in `EV-26 is approved by EV-29, which is missing.` So does a Revised line dated after the approval. A record that is system output, never signed or approved in its turn by another record carries no signature, so it approves nothing.

Training decks, quick reference cards, board MI packs, file copies of letters and most emails carry no signature by nature. The cover of such a file says so with a few words of what it is, in place of the Signed by line, and its Status is FINAL:

```
Never signed: training deck
```

Its ties count, and it puts no draft row on the list. It never counts toward a milestone, so listed beside signed files it neither signs the milestone nor holds it up. A milestone that lists only such files stays unsigned, with a reason that asks for the file that shows the milestone done.

A Signed by line that names a role wins over a Produced by, Approved by or Never signed line in the same cover, so a document someone should sign still needs its signature.

plan.md holds one row per milestone, and its Evidence cell lists every file that shows the milestone done. List the file that completes it, such as a lookback's final report, before that file exists, under an evidence id kept for it, such as EV-61. The check keeps the milestone unsigned while that file is missing, as in `Present, unsigned: EV-61 is missing.`, so a lookback two-thirds done never reads as signed on its methodology and approval alone. Mark the file that completes the milestone with `(done)` after its id, as in `EV-27, EV-28 (done)`, and reserve the id with its mark before the file exists. The milestone's date, and so its lateness, is then that file's signature or as-at date, and every other file the row lists still has to be present and signed, apart from a file never signed. A row with no mark keeps the newest date among its files. A row with two marks stops the check, which names its line.

The board's approval of the plan is an evidence file too, holding the minutes. Its `For:` line ends `E-PLAN-1`, as in `For: PLAN E-PLAN-1`, and it is FINAL and signed by the role that keeps the minutes, such as `Signed by: Company Secretary, 2026-02-10`. No milestone lists it. Until it counts as signed, every committed date reads `proposed`, the page asks the board for its approval of the plan and sign refuses. When the minutes are there and do not count, the Plan approval line gives the reason, such as `E-PLAN-1 changed since it was signed`. Once they count, the committed dates freeze. A date changed in plan.md afterwards shows as moved, lateness counts from the approved date, and the board is asked to approve the change. An added milestone asks the same, and neither stops the signature. A milestone taken out of plan.md afterwards does stop the signature, and sign gives the reason. Minutes signed again with a later date approve the plan as it then stands. The page keeps the date the board first approved beside each date it moved. The board summary flags a move only when the approval that first carried the new date came after the old date had passed, and the flag stays after later approvals.

Evidence arrives under the institution's own file names. Copy each file into evidence/, start its name with its evidence id and keep the institution's file name after the id, as in `EV-07 TM Alert Backlog MI - Mar 2026 v2 FINAL.xlsx`, then run `finding covers`. The id is one plan.md lists, E-PLAN-1 for the board's minutes, or an EV id. A file whose name starts with the institution's own reference number, such as CHG-2026-03952, gets no draft cover. Nor do two files under one id, such as a signed PDF beside the text file that already carries its id. The covers screen names each one with what to do.

A document sits behind a cover: `EV-07-procedure.pdf` has `EV-07-procedure.pdf.md` beside it, holding the four lines. `finding covers` reads each document and drafts its cover. The check reads a PDF with a text layer, a Word file, an Excel workbook (one page per visible sheet), a CSV, a saved .eml or a plain text file itself. It has no reader for any other file type, such as an Outlook .msg, so each cited page of one is typed into its cover as a scan's is, and `finding covers` drafts that cover saying so. A file the reader refuses, such as a Word file that still holds tracked changes, is typed the same way. The Source line of its draft cover says the check did not read it and why. The covers screen counts the words a reader cannot see that the reader left out of a page, and a row on that page gives the same count. The screen names up to five of them, as in `1 word a reader cannot see left out on page 1: "tial"`. A word on the deny list is counted and never printed. The reader leaves a Word file's comments out of its page, so the covers screen counts each comment that holds words on that file's line, as in `3 comments not read`. A page with no text, such as a scan, is typed into the cover under `## Page 7`, and the screen counts every tie that rests on typed text. Typing a page leaves the document's signature as it was. The signature covers the document and the cover's header lines other than Source and Checked by, and the cover's `Checked by:` line answers for the typed pages. A page typed or changed after a check has seen the cover is a change, and the check that first sees it keeps its date. The ties on the typed pages wait until the Checked by line carries that date or a later one. A change to the document itself, or to another header line, still needs a fresh signature date. The reader does no optical character recognition and reads no encrypted PDF. An Excel date reads as its serial number and a percent as its fraction, so those figures go on the list for a person.

## The verbs

From the kit root, where `finding/finding` is a two-line wrapper that runs `python3 -I finding/finding.py`:

```
finding/finding new ../findings/MRA-CMP-08
finding/finding check ../findings/MRA-CMP-08
finding/finding sign ../findings/MRA-CMP-08
```

Three more help around them, and `finding/finding --version` checks the files against the release:

```
finding/finding covers ../findings/MRA-CMP-08
finding/finding eval ../findings/MRA-CMP-08
finding/finding eval --library
finding/finding size ../findings/MRA-CMP-08
```

On Windows, type `py -I finding\finding.py` instead of `finding/finding`.

## Kinds of matter

finding.md names one of three kinds. A supervisory finding is one the Supervisor wrote, and only the Supervisor closes it. Internal audit closes an internal audit finding. A self-identified issue is a weakness the institution found on its own, and the institution's issue-management owner closes it, on the three `Issue closure` lines in closure/record.md. Internal audit tests the fix for all three. The issuer and the kind of matter freeze at the first check, so relabelling a finding afterwards is refused. A wrong kind at the very first check is caught only where the issuer names the Supervisor.

## Check

The check ties each figure, date and quotation to its cited page, and it does not compare documents with each other. So a list with no rows still leaves a reviewer to read for these:

- A version in force that is later than the one approved.
- Figures that disagree between documents.
- A scanned page that differs from the institution's other records.
- Work dated before the control that should come first, such as people working before their training.
- A status report that says more than its evidence.

Each milestone is not started, unsigned with the reason, or signed. A file counts as signed when it is FINAL, names a role and a date, and is unchanged since. A system output file counts the same way on its as-at date, for its milestone, for lateness and for sign, and its ties count like a signed file's. The milestone line names each one as produced by its system on that date, with no signature, so internal audit sees the difference, and a change to the file after that date unsigns it. A document approved by a separate record counts on that record's date, and the milestone line names the record, as in `EV-26 was approved by EV-29 on 2026-04-24.`, so internal audit can follow the chain. A change to the document after that date unsigns it. The line also names each listed file never signed, as in `Never signed: EV-30 (training deck).` The board's minutes need a signature of their own. A milestone below signed is SLIPPED once its date passes and AT RISK in the 14 days before. A milestone signed after its committed date is flagged on the board summary with how many days late, counted from the date of the file plan.md marks done, as in `Present on 2026-05-15, the date of EV-28, which plan.md marks done.` With no mark it counts from the newest signature or as-at date among the files, so a routine re-signature flags too. The quarterly progress starts at the quarter of the first committed date. Two evidence files with the same bytes, such as a scan saved under a second name, are named for the team under Needs a person, and `finding covers` names them too. Sign goes ahead with them. The board summary, commitment table and closure state follow. It refuses if the letter or the owner role changes after the first check, or if it would print a name on the deny list. A line that says the finding itself is closed, written before the closer's record exists, goes on the list as `closed in plan.md` or `closed in closure/memo.md`, and the rest of the page prints. That row stops the signature, and no ruling clears it, so the line has to be reworded. Any other use of the word closed, such as accounts closed in error, goes on the list the same way for the owner to rule on. A use is no row when the two words before closed and the two after it stand in that order in finding.md, as when the plan copies the letter's alerts closed without escalation. A line that says the finding itself is closed stays a row all the same. Every such row stays off the list once the closer's record exists. A wrong paste of the letter is corrected with `finding/finding check <folder> --repaste`, which keeps the evidence record, the deny list and the signature, and says so on every later page and in the log.

Each entry in closure/record.md, internal audit's, a closer's or the board's, counts once its reference, date and role each have a real form. A placeholder such as TBD, to follow or XXX counts for nothing, and so do a value under three characters, a reference with no digit and a date after the check. An entry dated before the first check counts, and its line says the check cannot see when it was made. A role is taken as written, such as Company Secretary or Head of Regulatory Relations. A name typed there prints as written, unless it is on the deny list, which stops the page.

In the memo, a cite such as `[EV-12 p2]` names page 2 of the file whose `For:` line ends `EV-12`. A heading such as `## Page 2` starts a page, and a file without one is one page. The kit's tie-out engine reads the cited page for each figure, date and quotation. A cite answers for its own sentence, even across a wrapped line, and a list item after a bullet or a list number is a sentence of its own. A quotation is read in double quote marks, or in single marks when it holds three words or more, and one with a bracketed insertion or an ellipsis goes on the list for a person. A cite written another way, such as `[EV-12, p2]`, `[ EV-12 p2 ]`, `[EV-12 pp. 1-2]` or `[EV-12 p2, EV-13 p1]`, is no cite, its page numbers are no claims, and its row names the form the check reads. A claim that does not tie goes on the list, as does a missing cite or one to a missing file, or to a file no milestone lists that is not signed. A section number is written as `2.`, `2)`, `(2)`, `2:` or `2 -`, or as `2.1` before a capitalised word, or is `1` or the number after the last heading's, as `## 3 Findings` after `## 2 Method`. The second cell is what the row prints after "To rule, name:", the claim and a short mark for its cite and sentence, so a ruling cannot clear a different claim:

A ruling of `fix the memo` or `fix the evidence` gets the same line while a row prints its claim under another mark. Once no row does, it stays in the file without a word.

`sign` runs only at a terminal, which stops a script by accident and proves nobody's identity. The institution's access controls supply that. A real finding is signed on the machine's date. `--today` works on sign only while the first line of finding.md is a shipped case's SYNTHETIC line, word for word. `finding new` writes no SYNTHETIC line, and on any other first line `sign` refuses `--today` with "drop --today". For: M2 EV-07
Signed by: Head of Complaints, 2026-03-14

Produced by: case manager aging report, 2026-04-30

A signature on that file dated after the last check that saw the file that went clears it, and a file under a new id is never held up. Once none of those holds, the check names the owner's signature first under Needs a person and prints the folder's fingerprint on a Ready to sign line, for internal audit to record what it tests. The signer types the owner role, then the first eight characters of a fingerprint over the memo, rulings, letter, plan, evidence, board approval and the tool's own code, including the engine and the document reader. The signature and the kit's release go into record.md. A later change to a covered file asks for a fresh signature. Entries the closers make in record.md do not, because they come after the signature: internal audit's, the Supervisor's and the issue-management owner's. When internal audit enters at least eight characters on `Internal audit tested fingerprint:`, the page compares them with the folder as it stands and asks for a fresh test if the folder moves on.

## The log

closure/finding-log.jsonl gets one line when `check --repaste` records a corrected paste of the letter, and the first such correction starts the file. After a lost state file, the next check adds a `record restarted` line only when closure/finding-log.jsonl is already there, and before then it writes no line. Every log line names the kind, the issuer and the first check.

## Measures

closure/measures.md holds what the Measures line on the check page counts, and no signature covers it. One line a month for hours and one line for each thing internal audit sends back:

```
Hours | 2026-10 | 38
Hours | 2026-11 | 12.5
Sent back | 2026-11-02 | Line 8 | the figure was the draft's | missed by the check
```

Part hours count, and so does the same line written as a table row. The check adds hours exactly and prints the total as it stands, such as 50.5 hours. A line that starts with Hours or Sent back and cannot be read, such as `Hours | 2026-11 | 1,240` or `Hours: 38`, is named on the page for the engagement team and counts for nothing.

## Fitting it to a financial institution

Two optional lists sit beside finding.md, or one folder up for the whole engagement. `denylist.txt` holds terms that must never print, one a line, matched in any letter case and with or without accents. `role-words.txt` holds ordinary words or phrases never to treat as a name, and a line there clears a term the check took for a name, even after a refused run. `denylist.txt` wins over it. A run of capitalised words that holds a document word, such as Procedure, Policy, Report, Plan, Minutes, Register or Methodology, is a title, so the check never takes it for a name, and the institution's file names can keep it. Every refusal over a term the check took from the letter offers role-words.txt, the refusal over a file name included, because renaming one of the institution's files breaks its link to the institution's records. A line can also clear one word of the institution's name, such as First in First Fenmoor Trust Bank, on the pages, and that word then passes in every form. The institution's full name never clears, so its refusal never offers the file. The check page prints only counts, as `Deny list: 3 names.`, and adds `; role-words.txt cleared 1 word of the institution's name.` when a line did. `finding/finding check <folder> --names` prints the names, for the person who asks.

The hours `finding size` assumes sit in a third optional file, `size-assumptions.txt`, in the same two places. It holds one line for each assumption the team has timed, and a line left out keeps the kit's value. A line beside the finding wins over the one in the folder above. The file changes no fingerprint, and `size` says how many lines it read. A folder of findings reads the file in that folder, and a finding's own file still wins for that finding, with its values named on the run's closing line. These are the kit's values:

```
minutes a claim by hand: 10
memo versions: 3
hours a status report: 2
minutes to find a signed file: 30
hours a rework round: 8
minutes a cover: 10
minutes a ruling: 15
minutes to read a claim: 10
rework rounds with the kit: 1
minutes a status report with the kit: 15
minutes to type and compare a page: 15
```

The templates, the plan columns and the record fields are constants at the top of finding.py. A column the institution adds to plan.md is read past wherever it sits, so it needs no change there. Renaming a column or a record field the check reads, or adding a kind of matter, needs a code change and a self-test case. A change to finding.py changes every fingerprint, and `python3 -I finding/release.py` refreshes RELEASE.json. With no version named it steps the kit to a site version, such as 0.7.1+site.1, so a kit changed at an institution never reads as the published release.

## Known limits

Each of these is open in 0.7.1 and can turn up in ordinary material, so a person reads for it.

- A person's name inside a title, such as the Natarajan Report, stays off the deny list, because a run holding a document word is a title. Put such a name in denylist.txt.
- An uncited claim in a lettered list such as a) or i), a middle-dot bullet or a table row borrows the cite on the next line, so it can tie.
- June of 2026 and the typo May. 22, 2026 are not read as dates, so a wrong one can pass.
- A month or a quarter ties any date inside it on its page. So a wrong month the page also shows, as in a monthly table, ties, as a wrong figure the page holds elsewhere does.
- A bracketed id such as (CP-07) reads as a misspelt cite, so the sentence's real cite is lost and its row asks for [CP-07].
- A cite written [EV-21 pp. 1, 2] or [EV-21 pages 1 and 2] gives each page number a row, and a cite after the point, as in (See [EV-21 p2].), or a point in i.e. leaves a claim with no cite.
- In Markdown evidence, an image's text, as in `![...](chart.png)`, and a link's title read as shown, so a figure found only there ties, and a placeholder of two or more words, such as `<Title Firstname Surname>`, leaves out the rest of its page, so that page's figures go on the list.
- A signed file swapped under a new evidence id with a backdated signature shows only as the old file gone, and not at all while the old file stays. When one of two identical documents is taken out, the other is named as filed under another id, and sign refuses it until it is signed again.
- In closure/record.md a reference such as IA-2026-TBC counts, while a two-letter role such as IA and a reference with no digit, such as BRC minutes (July), count for nothing.
- A person's name typed in a record role line prints as written unless it is on the deny list.

## Reference

A check exits 0 when nothing needs a person, 1 otherwise, and 2 on a usage error. An unsigned folder still needs its owner, so it exits 1. `--today YYYY-MM-DD` checks as of another date, and works on sign only as the Sign section says. `--names` and `--repaste` are the two options above. `python3 -I finding/selftest.py` tests the tool, including that the kit's own files import only modules on a fixed list and start no process.

name: read_file
result:
# Draft the covers

Goal: give each evidence file its header, so the check can count it and read it.

Reads: each file in evidence/, whose name starts with its evidence id and keeps the financial institution's file name after it, as in `EV-07 TM Alert Backlog MI - Mar 2026 v2 FINAL.xlsx`. The id is one plan.md lists, E-PLAN-1 for the board's minutes, or an EV id. Run `finding covers <folder>` first. It reads each PDF, Word file, Excel workbook, CSV, plain text file and email saved as .eml, writes a draft cover beside each one, and says which pages have no text. A file type it has no reader for, such as an Outlook .msg, gets a cover that says its pages are typed by a person. So does a file it refuses, such as a Word file that still holds tracked changes, and the cover's Source line gives the reason. A file whose name starts with any other id, such as the institution's reference number, gets no draft cover, and nor do two files under one id. The screen names each one.

Writes: the What and For lines of each cover, in a file beside the document named with `.md` added:

```text
What: EV-12 Quality review of reclassified complaints
For: M3 EV-12
Signed by:
Status: DRAFT
Source: read from the document by the check
```

## Rules

- What says what the document is, in the document's own words. Keep the evidence id first.
- For holds the milestone and ends in the evidence id. The id is the last word on the line, and memo cites use it.
- [finding/README.md](../finding/README.md#the-folder) says in one place when a cover takes Signed by, Produced by, Approved by or Never signed. The rules below say how a person fills each.
- Leave Signed by empty and Status at DRAFT. A person who has seen the signature types `Signed by: Head of Complaints, 2026-03-14` and sets `Status: FINAL`. An assistant never does.
- System output, such as a monthly MI workbook, a system aging report or a data extract, comes from a system as at a date. A person who has confirmed its as-at date replaces the Signed by line with `Produced by: case manager aging report, 2026-04-30`, naming the system or report that produced it, and sets `Status: FINAL`. The file then counts on that date, and the page says it was produced by that system with no signature. Never use the line for a document someone should sign, such as an attestation, minutes, a policy or a report a person issues, and an assistant never types it.
- An institution approves some documents by a separate record, such as a QA method approved by email, a lookback method approved on a signed sheet or an MI pack accepted in a resolved minute. # Draft the closure memo

Goal: write closure/memo.md, saying what was done, by whom and when, with a cite after every figure, date and quotation.

Reads: plan.md, the covers and the documents, each to its last page, because a later page may amend an earlier one. Reads the page before citing it.

Writes: closure/memo.md, one block per milestone, each opening with the milestone's id, with one sentence a line. The check counts a paragraph as one line, so every row on a long paragraph names the same line. With one sentence a line, a row on the list points at one sentence. This example ties in finding/cases/IA-CMP-02:

```text
M1, acknowledgement letters.
Since 2026-05-04 the complaint system sends the acknowledgement letter on the business day after a complaint is logged [EV-21 p1].
The Head of Complaints signed the procedure and sample on 2026-05-28 [EV-21 p2].

Tested control: M1, the acknowledgement letter procedure
Fix effective: 2026-05-04 [EV-21 p1]
Sample period: 2026-05-04 to 2026-05-22 [EV-21 p2]
```

## Rules

- Put a cite such as `[EV-07 p2]` straight after every figure, date and quotation. Its id is the last word of the file's For line. A PDF page is its printed page. A Word, CSV, email or text file is always p1, so the cite does not say where in the file a figure sits. A workbook page is a visible sheet, in workbook order, and hidden sheets, rows and columns do not count. An Excel percent or date reads as its stored fraction or serial number, so it goes on the list for a person.
- Write each cite exactly as `[EV-07 p2]`. A cite answers only for the sentence it sits in, even when a line wraps, so give every sentence that holds a claim its own cite. The page names a cite written another way, such as `[EV-07, p2]`, and reads it as no cite.
- Copy figures character for character from the cited page. Quote exactly, with straight double quotes, and quote two words or more. The check also reads a quotation in single quotes, straight or curly, when it holds three words or more. A quotation with a bracketed insertion or an ellipsis goes on the list for a person, so quote whole words where you can.
- Write every figure in digits and every date in full, as YYYY-MM-DD. The check reads no figure written in words, and no bare year, ordinal, month with no year, quarter label such as Q3, fiscal year such as FY26 or date with a two-digit year, so a claim written that way goes unchecked. A four-digit number from 1900 to 2099 reads as a year, so write a count such as 2,020 with its comma. A quarter with its year after it, such as Q3 2026 or 3Q 2026, is read as that quarter, and Excel's Aug-26 as August 2026. A number straight after version, v or Rev., such as version 3.1, is a label and needs no cite. The page names figures in words, years and two-digit-year dates on its `Not checked:` lines and leaves the rest to a reader.
- The claim count on the page is every date and quotation the check reads, and every number in digits that stands apart from letters. So a figure inside a quotation counts as well as the quotation, and so does the 6 in action 6. A number is joined to letters when a letter stands straight before it, or a letter and then a dash, slash or colon. Such a number is no claim, as in E11471, L2, S-07 or CHG-2026-04471. Other ids hold claims, so the 0173 in QA26Q2-0173, both numbers in 12345-6, the 11471 in ID 11471 and the 4471 in #4471 each count. A version number, a clock time, a list number in order and the forms the rule above says the check does not read are no claim. Nor is a section number or a part label such as Part 3 in a heading, as [finding/README.md](../finding/README.md#check) describes, though Part 3 in a sentence counts.
- Use one sentence per claim where you can, and start each sentence on a line of its own, so a row on the list points at one thing.
- Where a page holds two figures of one kind, such as two counts or two dates, quote the whole labelled line, so a figure moved to the other's place goes on the list.
- For each control internal audit will test, add a Tested control block with the date the fix took effect and the sample period, and cite each date to the page that holds it. Fix effective is the date the fix starts to bind, which can fall after the date it was approved or published. A date with no cite goes on the list, and so does a sample that starts before the fix. Nothing else goes in the block: the next line is read as ordinary memo text.
- Say what is unfinished, in plain words. Never say the finding is closed, because only the issuer closes a finding. Until the issuer's entry is in the record, such a line is a row on the list that stops the signature, and no ruling clears it, so it has to be reworded. Any other use of the word closed, such as accounts closed in error, goes on the list for the owner to rule on, so use it only where the evidence does. A use in the letter's own words, such as alerts closed without escalation copied from a required action, is no row.
- Leave signature state to the screen, and write what the documents show. A sentence such as "no cover is signed" turns false once a person signs.
- Write no reason why a row should be cleared into the memo. That is the next job.

## Passing

`finding check` prints the list. Until the covers are signed, a clean draft leaves one row for each draft cover, which waits on a person's signature, and rows a person has to decide. A claim that does not match its page keeps its own row, so fix it before handing over. Then run `finding eval <folder>`, which plants errors in memory and shows what the check would catch and what a person still has to read for. A figure in the right sentence that is wrong but sits on the cited page ties, so a reviewer reads each sentence against its page.

```

# The finding owner

This page is for the person on the business side who owns a finding, such as the Head of Complaints in the invented case MRA-CMP-07. The tool asks two things of you. You rule on each row the check could not tie, and once nothing is left you sign.

The check is plain code with no AI model in it, so one folder checked as of one date always prints the same page. It looks for each figure, date and quotation in the closure memo on the evidence page its cite names. Whether the fix works is left to you, internal audit and the issuer.

## The page you read

From the root folder of the repository:

```sh
python3 -I finding/finding.py check finding/cases/MRA-CMP-07 --today 2026-11-04
```

The `--today` option fixes the date so your screen matches this one, trimmed where it shows `...`:

```text
Finding MRA-CMP-07, a supervisory finding from the Supervisor dated 2026-01-15. Owner: Head of Complaints. Checked as of 2026-11-04, kit release 0.7.1.
...
Memo check: 13 claims, 7 tie, 3 on the list, 1 cleared.
  Line 8: 1,248 is cited to EV-07 p2, and the page does not hold it; the nearest figures on the page are 1,284 and 2. To rule, name: 1,248 #972adb19
  Line 10: EV-12, which is a draft, holds 4 claims, on lines 10, 15 and 16, that match its pages and wait on a person's signature. To rule, name: EV-12 draft #81b3b231
  Line 16: the sample period for M2 starts 2026-01-05, before the fix took effect on 2026-03-17, so the sample mixes items from before and after the fix. To rule, name: sample period for M2 #106ddd50
  Cleared: line 8, March 2026, by the Head of Complaints on 2026-11-04: The page says January to March, and the plan year is 2026.
  7 ties rest on text a person typed: 7 in plain-text evidence, none on a page typed into a cover.
  Not checked: 1 figure written in words, line 6 (three).
Signature: none yet.
...
Needs a person:
  Head of Complaints: M2, the list (3 rows).
...
```

The Owner field names the role your rulings and signature must carry. The command exits 1 while anyone still has something to do.

## What each row means

Each row opens with the memo line it concerns, and a row you can rule on ends with the words a ruling uses to name it.

- Line 8 says 1,248 and the cited page says 1,284, which looks like two digits swapped in typing. The memo is wrong.
- Line 10 is one row for a draft. The quality review EV-12 supports four claims in the memo, and they wait until someone signs it.
- Line 16 says the tested sample starts before the fix took effect, so it mixes items from both sides of the fix.

Other rows name a missing cite, a cite to a file that is not there, or a page with no text that someone has to type. No ruling clears a row for a memo or plan that calls the finding closed before the closer has recorded it, so someone rewords the line.

Below the rows, each Cleared line gives the role, date and reason of a past ruling. The Not checked line names figures the check skipped, such as a number written in words.

## How to rule

A ruling is one line in closure/rulings.md. It gives the memo line, the name the row prints at its end, the ruling, your role, a date and a reason.

```text
Line 16 | sample period for M2 #106ddd50 | cleared | Head of Complaints | 2026-11-04 | Items from before 2026-03-17 were drawn on purpose as a baseline error rate.
```

A `cleared` ruling takes the row off the list and prints your reason on every later page. To send a row back, rule `fix the memo`, or `fix the evidence` when a document must change or be signed again. # Testing a closure package

This guide is for internal audit, model risk and anyone else the financial institution asks to test a closure package that RegRem Engine helped prepare. The check is deterministic code with no AI model inside, so a rerun on the same folder and date gives the page the team got. You can also make it fail on purpose before you rely on it. It looks for each figure and date written in digits, and each quotation, on the evidence page its cite names. Whether the fix works stays with you.

Run the commands from the kit root, the folder that holds finding/. They use the invented case IA-CMP-02, and on a real package you give the folder's own path. Windows users run `py -I finding\finding.py` in place of `finding/finding`.

## A half-day test plan

### 1. Copy the folder (15 minutes)

Work on a copy kept on a machine the institution approves. Copy the whole folder, so the hidden `.finding-state.json` that records which files were signed comes too. A copy made with `cp -R folder/* copy` leaves it behind.

```sh
cp -R finding/cases/IA-CMP-02 audit-02
```

### 2. Confirm the release (5 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding --version
```

On the published kit it reports that every file matches the release. A changed kit names each changed file or shows a site version such as 0.7.1+site.1. Then ask the team for the institution's log of each change.

### 3. Rerun the check and confirm the fingerprint (30 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding check audit-02
```

Your list should match the one the team showed you. The fingerprint is a hash of the letter, plan, evidence, memo, rulings and board approval, plus the tool's own code. This unsigned case prints it last, as `Ready to sign: the folder's fingerprint is e8196695.` A signed folder prints it on the signed line, and a `Changed since signing:` line names any covered file edited since. Compare the eight characters with the Fingerprint line in closure/record.md. For a second test, add `Internal audit tested fingerprint: e8196695` to the copy's record.md and check again. A match adds nothing to the page, and a mismatch names both values and asks internal audit for a fresh test.

### 4. Run the eval (20 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding eval audit-02
```

The eval plants one error at a time in a copy of the memo held in memory, and leaves the folder untouched. On this case it ends `Caught 30 of 38.` It caught every changed digit, swapped pair of digits and moved date. It caught none of the 6 figures replaced by another figure from the same page, and 11 of the 13 cites moved to another page. Each miss is listed by memo line for your workpaper.

### 5. Run the library (10 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding eval --library
```

It should report 21 cases, all as expected, 6 of them a known limit. Each known-limit case writes down something the check cannot see.

### 6. Plant your own errors (60 minutes)

The eval knows only six kinds of error and used five on this memo, so change the copy's memo yourself five to ten times. The command below plants six errors. They are two swapped digits, a moved date, a wrong month, a figure taken from elsewhere on the page, a changed quotation and a cite moved to another page.

```sh
sed -e 's/118 were/181 were/' \
    -e 's/on 2026-06-29/on 2026-06-19/' \
    -e 's/covers May 2026/covers June 2026/' \
    -e 's/402 of 410/410 of 410/' \
    -e 's/a deputy covers absence/the deputy "covers when the manager is on leave"/' \
    -e 's/2026-05-28 \[EV-21 p2\]/2026-05-28 [EV-21 p1]/' \
    audit-02/closure/memo.md > audit-02/memo.new
mv audit-02/memo.new audit-02/closure/memo.md
finding/finding check audit-02
```

The memo check now reads `14 claims, 9 tie, 5 on the list.` The quotation row shows the words the page holds. The second 410 still ties, because 410 appears on the cited page. The page also reports that the folder no longer matches the fingerprint you entered in step 3. Record 5 caught of 6 planted, with the release and the fingerprint from step 3.

### 7. Read for what the check cannot see (90 minutes)

An empty list means every claim was found on its cited page. A person still reads for five things:

- A version in force that is later than the version the institution approved.
- Figures that disagree between two documents, since each can tie to its own page.
- A scanned page whose typed text disagrees with the institution's own records.
- Work done before the control meant to precede it, such as staff handling complaints before their training.
- A status report claiming more than its evidence supports.

Read each sentence against its page too. A wrong figure the page also holds ties, as step 6 showed. So does a wrong month when the page lists that month too, as a monthly table does. The `Not checked:` line names figures written in words, bare years and dates with two-digit years. The page also counts ties that rest on text a person typed. In the invented cases every tie counts as typed, because the evidence is plain text and the check cannot tell an export from retyping. Put every typed tie in your sample. Compare the claim count with the memo's length, because a memo that makes no checkable claim still gets an empty list and a Ready to sign line.

### 8. Record the test (15 minutes)

In the live folder's closure/record.md, fill internal audit's reference, date and role, and put at least eight characters of the tested fingerprint on `Internal audit tested fingerprint:`. The owner's signature stands when you add them. If the folder changes later, every check asks internal audit to test again. When you send something back, someone on the team adds a `Sent back` line to closure/measures.md. A line ending `missed by the check` marks an item the check had passed, and the check page counts both.

## Limits

Every case here is invented, and the kit has not been run on a real finding. The counts above come from one small invented memo and predict nothing about your institution's papers. The check is a floor under a reviewer's reading. Whether the fix works, and whether the finding closes, stays with internal audit and the issuer.

finding/finding --version
```

On the published kit it reports that every file matches the release. A changed kit names each changed file or shows a site version such as 0.7.1+site.1. Then ask the team for the institution's log of each change.

### 3. Rerun the check and confirm the fingerprint (30 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding check audit-02
```

Your list should match the one the team showed you. The fingerprint is a hash of the letter, plan, evidence, memo, rulings and board approval, plus the tool's own code. This unsigned case prints it last, as `Ready to sign: the folder's fingerprint is e8196695.` A signed folder prints it on the signed line, and a `Changed since signing:` line names any covered file edited since. Compare the eight characters with the Fingerprint line in closure/record.md. For a second test, add `Internal audit tested fingerprint: e8196695` to the copy's record.md and check again. A match adds nothing to the page, and a mismatch names both values and asks internal audit for a fresh test.

### 4. Run the eval (20 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding eval audit-02
```

The eval plants one error at a time in a copy of the memo held in memory, and leaves the folder untouched. On this case it ends `Caught 30 of 38.` It caught every changed digit, swapped pair of digits and moved date. It caught none of the 6 figures replaced by another figure from the same page, and 11 of the 13 cites moved to another page. Each miss is listed by memo line for your workpaper.

### 5. Run the library (10 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding eval --library
```

It should report 21 cases, all as expected, 6 of them a known limit. Each known-limit case writes down something the check cannot see.

### 6. Plant your own errors (60 minutes)

The eval knows only six kinds of error and used five on this memo, so change the copy's memo yourself five to ten times. The command below plants six errors. They are two swapped digits, a moved date, a wrong month, a figure taken from elsewhere on the page, a changed quotation and a cite moved to another page.

```sh

    -e 's/on 2026-06-29/on 2026-06-19/' \
    -e 's/covers May 2026/covers June 2026/' \
    -e 's/402 of 410/410 of 410/' \
    -e 's/a deputy covers absence/the deputy "covers when the manager is on leave"/' \
    -e 's/2026-05-28 \[EV-21 p2\]/2026-05-28 [EV-21 p1]/' \
    audit-02/closure/memo.md > audit-02/memo.new
mv audit-02/memo.new audit-02/closure/memo.md
finding/finding check audit-02
```

The memo check now reads `14 claims, 9 tie, 5 on the list.` The quotation row shows the words the page holds. The second 410 still ties, because 410 appears on the cited page. The page also reports that the folder no longer matches the fingerprint you entered in step 3. Record 5 caught of 6 planted, with the release and the fingerprint from step 3.

### 7. Read for what the check cannot see (90 minutes)

An empty list means every claim was found on its cited page. A person still reads for five things:

- A version in force that is later than the version the institution approved.
- Figures that disagree between two documents, since each can tie to its own page.
- A scanned page whose typed text disagrees with the institution's own records.
- Work done before the control meant to precede it, such as staff handling complaints before their training.
- A status report claiming more than its evidence supports.

Read each sentence against its page too. A wrong figure the page also holds ties, as step 6 showed. So does a wrong month when the page lists that month too, as a monthly table does. The `Not checked:` line names figures written in words, bare years and dates with two-digit years. The page also counts ties that rest on text a person typed. In the invented cases every tie counts as typed, because the evidence is plain text and the check cannot tell an export from retyping. Put every typed tie in your sample. Compare the claim count with the memo's length, because a memo that makes no checkable claim still gets an empty list and a Ready to sign line.

### 8. Record the test (15 minutes)

In the live folder's closure/record.md, fill internal audit's reference, date and role, and put at least eight characters of the tested fingerprint on `Internal audit tested fingerprint:`. The owner's signature stands when you add them. If the folder changes later, every check asks internal audit to test again. When you send something back, someone on the team adds a `Sent back` line to closure/measures.md. A line ending `missed by the check` marks an item the check had passed, and the check page counts both.

## Limits

Every case here is invented, and the kit has not been run on a real finding. The counts above come from one small invented memo and predict nothing about your institution's papers. The check is a floor under a reviewer's reading. Whether the fix works, and whether the finding closes, stays with internal audit and the issuer.

# An engineer's first week

This page is for the one engineer, on a financial institution's staff or brought in by it, who fits RegRem Engine to that institution in a week. By day 5 the tool runs on the institution's approved machine and refuses to print any name on its deny list. You also know which of the institution's evidence formats it reads, and any code change shows as a site version. Every case and name below is invented.

Every command here runs from the kit root, where finding/ sits. Windows users replace `finding/finding` with `py -I finding\finding.py`. Keep findings beside the kit, such as in `../findings`, because `finding new` refuses a path inside it.

## Day 1: run it on the invented cases

On the approved machine, confirm the copy matches its release and passes both self-tests:

```sh
finding/finding --version
python3 -I finding/selftest.py
python3 -I tieout/selftest.py
```

Expect `RegRem Engine 0.7.1`, then `selftest: PASS (1166 expectations)` and `selftest: PASS (77 expectations)`. Save a baseline outside the kit, checking a copy of the case. A check with a new date rewrites a shipped case's state file, and `--version` then names it as a changed test file.

```sh
mkdir -p ../acceptance/cases
cp -R finding/cases/MRA-CMP-07 ../acceptance/cases/
finding/finding check ../acceptance/cases/MRA-CMP-07 --today 2026-11-04 > ../acceptance/MRA-CMP-07.txt
finding/finding eval finding/cases/IA-CMP-02 > ../acceptance/eval-IA-CMP-02.txt
finding/finding eval --library > ../acceptance/library.txt
```

Pass the same `--today` each time you save a check, or the day counts on the milestone lines will differ. The eval catches 30 of 38 planted errors, and the library reports all 21 cases as expected, 6 of them known limits.

## Day 2: the deny list and role words

Run `finding/finding new ../findings/TRY-01` and fill finding.md and plan.md with an invented letter in the institution's style, using its role titles and system names. Then:

```sh
finding/finding check ../findings/TRY-01 --today 2026-11-04
finding/finding check ../findings/TRY-01 --names
```

The first full check puts the institution's name and its distinctive words on the deny list. It also adds runs of capitalised words from the letter, such as a system's name. Pages print only a count, and `--names` prints the list.

Ask the finding owner's office for every term that must never print, such as legal and trading names, systems and projects. Write them one a line in `denylist.txt`, beside finding.md for one finding or in `../findings/` for all of them. Matching ignores case and accents.

Ordinary words the check collected, such as a team called Records Desk, go in `role-words.txt` in either place. The page then reads `Deny list: 6 names; role-words.txt left out 1.` The deny list wins over role words, and the institution's full name never clears. One word in `role-words.txt` clears every run holding it, so the owner's office reads the `--names` output.

## Day 3: evidence and size assumptions

Copy invented documents in the institution's real formats into evidence/, each name starting with its evidence id, and draft the covers:

```sh
finding/finding covers ../findings/TRY-01
```

A file name holding a deny-list term stops it. In a trial run, `EV-02 Case Tracker aging export.csv` was refused, and covers ran once Case Tracker went into `role-words.txt`. Put a system name there only when the owner's office agrees it may print, because renaming the file instead breaks its link to the institution's records.

`finding size` prints assumed hours by hand and with the kit. Put timed figures in `size-assumptions.txt`, beside the finding or one folder up, using the wording in finding/README.md:

```text
minutes a claim by hand: 12
hours a status report: 3
```

`finding/finding size ../findings` then says how many values came from the file. The file changes no fingerprint and no release hash.

## Day 4: templates and record fields

A plan column the institution adds needs no code, because the check reads past it. Templates, plan columns and record fields are constants near the top of `finding/finding.py`, such as TEMPLATE_PLAN, PLAN_COLUMNS and RECORD_FIELDS. A new record line goes in both RECORD_FIELDS and TEMPLATE_RECORD. The owner's signature covers it unless it is also added to UNSIGNED_RECORD_FIELDS, and the page prints nothing from it until code does. Renaming a field the check reads needs code and a self-test case.

Then refresh the release file:

```sh
finding/finding --version
python3 -I finding/release.py
```

Before the refresh, `--version` prints `Changed since this release: finding/finding.py.`, each check page names the file, and the self-test fails. The refresh prints `RELEASE.json: 0.7.1+site.1, 8 files, 45 test files`, and a later change steps to 0.7.1+site.2. From then on every full check page and every signature names the site version. Copy RELEASE.json aside before each refresh to keep the old hashes.

A code change moves every fingerprint too, so make it between findings, before anyone signs.

## Day 5: acceptance and the log

Someone other than you accepts each change by rerunning three things:

1. Both self-tests from day 1 end in PASS.
2. The library run still shows 21 of 21 cases as expected.
3. The day 1 screen matches, apart from the intended change:

```sh
finding/finding check ../acceptance/cases/MRA-CMP-07 --today 2026-11-04 > ../acceptance/MRA-CMP-07-site.txt
diff ../acceptance/MRA-CMP-07.txt ../acceptance/MRA-CMP-07-site.txt
```

In a trial that added one plan template line and one record field, only the release on the Finding line differed. A change to what the tool prints also means editing the expected screens in `finding/selftest.py`, and the accepter reads that edit.

The tool keeps no log of site changes. Keep one page inside the institution with each site version, its date, the reason and the accepter. Add the hashes before and after, the release that signed each folder and which of the institution's roles owns the kit.

## What stays open

The check ties each figure, date in digits and quotation to its own cited page, with no AI inside. It never compares documents, so two that disagree can both pass, and a wrong figure on the cited page ties. Whether a fix is right stays with people. Internal audit tests the fix, and only the issuer closes the finding. The tool has never run on a real finding.

# Running a finding week to week

This page is for the preparer who keeps a live finding's folder, the reviewer who reads its memo and the owner who rules and signs. It follows the invented case MRA-CMP-07 through the week of Monday 2026-11-16, with a board pack due on Thursday 2026-11-19.

Commands run from the kit root. On Windows, `py -I finding\finding.py` replaces `finding/finding` and File Explorer does the copies. The examples pass `--today` so your screen matches, and a live folder leaves it off so the check uses the machine's date. To follow along, copy the case outside the kit:

```sh
mkdir -p ../findings
cp -R finding/cases/MRA-CMP-07 ../findings/MRA-CMP-07
mkdir ../findings/MRA-CMP-07/closure/pages
```

## Monday: check, and keep the page

The preparer confirms the release, then saves the check's page under the day's date:

```sh
finding/finding --version
finding/finding check ../findings/MRA-CMP-07 --today 2026-11-16 > ../findings/MRA-CMP-07/closure/pages/2026-11-16.txt
```

The first command should end `Every file matches this release.` A page saved in closure/pages/ changes neither later pages nor the folder's fingerprint. The check exits 1 while anything waits on a person.

The page's last block, Needs a person, sorts the open work by role for the status call. This Monday it gives M2 and three list rows to the Head of Complaints, M3 to the Complaints QA lead and M4 to the Head of Digital. On the list sit a figure typed as 1,248 where page 2 of EV-07 says 1,284, a draft quality review, and a sample that starts before its fix.

## Tuesday: the owner rules

A ruling line gives the memo line, the text the row prints after "To rule, name:", one of `cleared`, `fix the memo` or `fix the evidence`, the owner role, a date and a reason:

```text
Line 8 | 1,248 #972adb19 | fix the memo | Head of Complaints | 2026-11-17 | The page says 1,284.
Line 16 | sample period for M2 #106ddd50 | cleared | Head of Complaints | 2026-11-17 | The owner drew this sample across the fix date to compare error rates.
```

The owner, or the preparer on the owner's word, appends these to closure/rulings.md. A ruling dated after the check that reads it counts for nothing. Only `cleared` takes a row off the list, and the check accepts it on any row that prints a name. So the owner never clears a wrong figure, which the memo has to fix. Clearing the draft row would leave M3 unsigned, so it waits for the QA lead's signature. An AI assistant may draft proposals into closure/proposed-rulings.md, a file the check ignores.

## Wednesday: fixes land

The preparer edits line 8 of closure/memo.md to read 1,284. That changes the sentence, so the March 2026 row on that line returns under a new mark, `March 2026 #ffa37a3f`, and the page says `Ruling at rulings.md line 4 names no row` about the old ruling. While a sentence and its cite stay the same, a ruling follows its claim to any line, so the owner need not wait for the memo to settle. This sentence changed, so the owner rules on the new mark:

```text
Line 8 | March 2026 #ffa37a3f | cleared | Head of Complaints | 2026-11-18 | Page 2 gives the period as January to March, in plan year 2026.
```

Someone who has seen the QA lead's signature changes the EV-12 cover to `Signed by: Complaints QA lead, 2026-11-18` and `Status: FINAL`. An assistant never types either line. After any real change to the memo, run the eval:

```sh
finding/finding eval ../findings/MRA-CMP-07
```

It plants errors in memory and lists each one the check let through. This week it caught 26 of 31, and one miss reads `Line 10: 31 changed to 240 still ties.` The reviewer starts from that list.

## Thursday: the board cutoff

The preparer checks again, saves the page and compares it with Monday's. On Windows, `fc` compares two files.

```sh
finding/finding check ../findings/MRA-CMP-07 --today 2026-11-19 > ../findings/MRA-CMP-07/closure/pages/2026-11-19.txt
diff ../findings/MRA-CMP-07/closure/pages/2026-11-16.txt ../findings/MRA-CMP-07/closure/pages/2026-11-19.txt
```

The list is now empty, and the board summary reports the late signature on M3:

```text
Flagged commitments: M2 slipped 249 days, M3 signed 202 days after its commitment, M4 slipped 142 days.
Memo check: 13 claims, 12 tie, 0 on the list, 2 cleared.
```

Anything still under Needs a person at the cutoff goes to the role it names. The board summary is a draft, and the finding owner decides what reaches the pack.

## Friday: measures

The preparer records this week's booked hours in closure/measures.md, plus one line per item internal audit returned. The next page counts both on its Measures line.

```text
Hours | 2026-11 | 6.5
Sent back | 2026-11-20 | Line 10 | the memo still called the review a draft | missed by the check
```

## How a slipped milestone shows

Below signed, a milestone reads AT RISK in the 14 days before its committed date and SLIPPED after it, with a day count. Signed board minutes freeze the committed dates. Move M4 to 2026-12-31 in plan.md and the page still counts from the approved date, and asks the board to approve the change:

```text
committed 2026-06-30, moved to 2026-12-31 in plan.md after the board approved the plan. Not started. SLIPPED by 142 days.
```

Once the minutes are signed again with a later date, the new date counts. The board summary keeps a note that M4 moved after 2026-06-30 had passed, so re-dating never hides a slip.

## Who acts on what

- The preparer runs the check on Monday and Thursday, runs `finding/finding covers` the day a file arrives, fixes memo rows, types accepted rulings and keeps measures.md.
- Each milestone owner named under Needs a person gets the file signed, or signed again after a revision.
- The finding owner rules on every row, decides what goes to the board and signs last.
- The reviewer is someone who wrote no part of the memo. Before the pack, they compare every sentence with its cited page, then read every Cleared line, the eval's misses, the `Not checked:` lines and any typed page.

## Limits

With the list empty, every claim the check reads sits on its cited page or carries the owner's ruling. The check holds no AI model, so one folder checked as of one date gives the same page on every run. It reads each claim against its own cite only. Two documents can disagree and both pass, and a wrong figure that also appears on the cited page ties. On this Thursday, memo line 10 still said the review "is still a draft and carries no signature", and the page raised nothing. The check does not judge whether the fix works. Internal audit tests that, and only the issuer closes the finding. Every case here is invented, and the tool has never run on a real finding.

Clearing the draft row would leave M3 unsigned, so it waits for the QA lead's signature. An AI assistant may draft proposals into closure/proposed-rulings.md, a file the check ignores.

## Wednesday: fixes land

The preparer edits line 8 of closure/memo.md to read 1,284. That changes the sentence, so the March 2026 row on that line returns under a new mark, `March 2026 #ffa37a3f`, and the page says `Ruling at rulings.md line 4 names no row` about the old ruling. While a sentence and its cite stay the same, a ruling follows its claim to any line, so the owner need not wait for the memo to settle. This sentence changed, so the owner rules on the new mark:

```text
Line 8 | March 2026 #ffa37a3f | cleared | Head of Complaints | 2026-11-18 | Page 2 gives the period as January to March, in plan year 2026.
```

Someone who has seen the QA lead's signature changes the EV-12 cover to `Signed by: Complaints QA lead, 2026-11-18` and `Status: FINAL`. An assistant never types either line. After any real change to the memo, run the eval:

```sh
finding/finding eval ../findings/MRA-CMP-07
```

It plants errors in memory and lists each one the check let through. This week it caught 26 of 31, and one miss reads `Line 10: 31 changed to 240 still ties.` The reviewer starts from that list.

## Thursday: the board cutoff

The preparer checks again, saves the page and compares it with Monday's. On Windows, `fc` compares two files.

```sh
finding/finding check ../findings/MRA-CMP-07 --today 2026-11-19 > ../findings/MRA-CMP-07/closure/pages/2026-11-19.txt
diff ../findings/MRA-CMP-07/closure/pages/2026-11-16.txt ../findings/MRA-CMP-07/closure/pages/2026-11-19.txt
```

The list is now empty, and the board summary reports the late signature on M3:

```text
Flagged commitments: M2 slipped 249 days, M3 signed 202 days after its commitment, M4 slipped 142 days.
Memo check: 13 claims, 12 tie, 0 on the list, 2 cleared.
```

Anything still under Needs a person at the cutoff goes to the role it names. The board summary is a draft, and the finding owner decides what reaches the pack.

## Friday: measures

The preparer records this week's booked hours in closure/measures.md, plus one line per item internal audit returned. The next page counts both on its Measures line.

```text
Hours | 2026-11 | 6.5
Sent back | 2026-11-20 | Line 10 | the memo still called the review a draft | missed by the check
```

## How a slipped milestone shows

Below signed, a milestone reads AT RISK in the 14 days before its committed date and SLIPPED after it, with a day count. Signed board minutes freeze the committed dates. Move M4 to 2026-12-31 in plan.md and the page still counts from the approved date, and asks the board to approve the change:

```text
committed 2026-06-30, moved to 2026-12-31 in plan.md after the board approved the plan. Not started. SLIPPED by 142 days.
```

Once the minutes are signed again with a later date, the new date counts. The board summary keeps a note that M4 moved after 2026-06-30 had passed, so re-dating never hides a slip.

## Who acts on what

- The preparer runs the check on Monday and Thursday, runs `finding/finding covers` the day a file arrives, fixes memo rows, types accepted rulings and keeps measures.md.
- Each milestone owner named under Needs a person gets the file signed, or signed again after a revision.
- The finding owner rules on every row, decides what goes to the board and signs last.
- The reviewer is someone who wrote no part of the memo. Before the pack, they compare every sentence with its cited page, then read every Cleared line, the eval's misses, the `Not checked:` lines and any typed page.

## Limits

With the list empty, every claim the check reads sits on its cited page or carries the owner's ruling. The check holds no AI model, so one folder checked as of one date gives the same page on every run. It reads each claim against its own cite only. Two documents can disagree and both pass, and a wrong figure that also appears on the cited page ties. On this Thursday, memo line 10 still said the review "is still a draft and carries no signature", and the page raised nothing. The check does not judge whether the fix works. Internal audit tests that, and only the issuer closes the finding. Every case here is invented, and the tool has never run on a real finding.

# finding: the walk

Run every command from the kit root, the folder that holds finding/. On Windows, type `py -I finding\finding.py` wherever this page says `finding/finding`, and do the copies and edits in File Explorer and a text editor. The walk uses `--today 2026-11-04` so your screen matches this page.

## 1. The line that opens every screen

Every check, and every refusal about a finding, starts with this line:

```
This folder may hold confidential supervisory information. Keep it on a machine the institution has approved, and share nothing from it outside the institution.
```

`finding/finding new ../findings/DEMO-01` run a second time prints only its refusal, `Refused: ../findings/DEMO-01 already exists.`, because it has read no finding, and so does `new` on a path inside the kit. The tool sends nothing anywhere. Keeping the folder on an approved machine is up to the people using it.

## 2. Open a finding

```
finding/finding new ../findings/DEMO-01
```

It prints `Made ../findings/DEMO-01. Fill the header lines in finding.md and paste each part of the letter under its heading, then fill plan.md.` and makes `DEMO-01/` in a findings folder beside the kit, with finding.md, plan.md, an empty evidence/, and closure/ with its memo, record, rulings and measures templates. No template holds a SYNTHETIC line to delete. The last part of the path is the finding's id. A folder inside the kit is refused, so `finding/finding new DEMO-01` from the kit root prints `Refused: DEMO-01 is inside the kit's own folders. Make the finding folder outside the kit, such as ../findings/DEMO-01 from the kit root.` To see what to fill first, check the empty folder:

```
finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-01
```

It prints the opening line, then `Not ready: finding.md has no Institution yet. Fill that line, then check again.` and exits 1, because the header lines are empty. Remove the folder when you have seen enough:

```
rm -r ../findings/DEMO-01
```

## 2b. From a letter to a first check

A real letter has no such headings, so a person fills the header lines and puts each passage under the heading it answers. Here is a short invented letter in that shape, with one milestone:

```
finding/finding new ../findings/DEMO-02
cat > ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.md <<'END'
# Finding DEMO-02
Identifier: DEMO-02
Institution: Harbour Example Bank
Issuer: the Supervisor
Letter date: 2026-09-14
Kind of matter: supervisory finding
Owner role: Head of Complaints

## Concern
Complaint files are not kept for the full period.

## Cause
No procedure sets the retention period.

## Consequence
Files the Supervisor asked for could not be found.

## Corrective action
Set the period in a procedure and move the files.

## Commitment
Report progress to the Supervisor within 60 days.
END
echo '| M1 Issue the retention procedure | Head of Complaints | 2027-01-31 | The procedure sets the period | EV-01 | A sample of files meets the period |' >> ../findings/DEMO-02/plan.md
finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-02 --today 2026-11-04
```

It prints the full screen, opening with this and ending with what needs a person:

```
Finding DEMO-02, a supervisory finding from the Supervisor dated 2026-09-14. Owner: Head of Complaints. Checked as of 2026-11-04, kit release 0.7.1.

Milestones
M1 Issue the retention procedure. Head of Complaints, committed 2027-01-31 proposed. Not started.
```

That first full check fixes the letter's text. Change a word and check again:

```
sed 's/for the full period/for the whole period/' ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.md > ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.new
mv ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.new ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.md
finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-02 --today 2026-11-04
```

```
Refused: the Concern in finding.md is not the text first checked on 2026-11-04. The Supervisor's words do not change; restore them, or run check --repaste if the first paste was wrong.
```

If the first paste was wrong, `finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-02 --repaste --today 2026-11-04` records the correction and keeps the evidence record, the deny list and any signature. Every later page says the text was corrected and on what date, and the folder's log holds the line.

The first check also puts the financial institution's name and any run of two or three capitalised words from the letter on the deny list, and a page that would print one is refused. A run that holds a role word or a document word, such as Head or Procedure, is a title and stays off the list, so an institution's file named for a procedure the letter cites keeps its name. If a term on the list is an ordinary word or a title, the refusal says to add it to `role-words.txt` beside finding.md, and the next check clears it. That holds when the term sits in the name of one of the institution's files too, because renaming the file breaks its link to the institution's records. A word of the institution's name clears the same way, and the page then counts it. The institution's full name never clears, so its refusal does not offer the file. `finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-02 --names` prints the list, for the person who asks. Every other page prints only its count. Remove the folder:

```
rm -r ../findings/DEMO-02
```

## 4. Change a signed file

Steps 4 and 5 work on a copy, so the shipped case stays as it is. Copy the case, keep a copy of EV-03, the signed taxonomy, change one word of its body, and check again:

```
